proposed.note: Wideband emitter pushes busy-energy-without-preamble high and makes every scanned channel equally bad (low inter-channel spread) — direct emitter evidence, not a symptom-only call.
Selective emitter raises noise/energy on only some channels, so a scan shows a few very hot channels among clean ones (high inter-channel spread) unlike barrage's uniform hit.

A sweeping jammer periodically revisits channels, so scans show a periodic bad-channel pattern together with elevated non-preamble energy — no example in the label set, kept conservative on positive emitter evidence.

Deep multipath/distance fades cause outages (high silent loss, high shadow-loss) with PDR still tracking RSSI reasonably; critically there is no raised noise floor, no non-preamble energy, and no hot channels in scan, so it must not be called jamming.
A dropped/dead node stops answering heartbeats entirely on one link (long heartbeat gap plus strong link asymmetry) while the spectrum itself is clean, ruling out an RF cause.

Loss concentrated on one asymmetric link with a shadow-loss signature (collisions the sender's own CCA never saw) and no noise-floor rise points to an unseen third node colliding at the receiver, not an emitter.

A reactive jammer keys up as soon as it senses the node's own transmission, so the node's local channel-access logic sees the channel busy and its defer time rises, yet mesh heartbeats keep flowing normally (no missed peers) and PDR stays correlated with own RSSI, unlike a hidden or dead node.

Congestion is self-inflicted: loss tracks the node's own offered load while there is no emitter evidence at all (flat noise floor, no non-preamble energy) — the canonical congestion signature even though loss_load_corr happened to be flat in the labelled snapshot.
